s: The most advanced open-source relational database: ACID, rich types, extensibility, and standards compliance.
w: MVCC provides concurrent reads/writes without locks. B-tree/hash/GiST/GIN/BRIN indexes support diverse query patterns. JSONB columns bridge document and relational models. Streaming replication (sync/async) and logical replication enable read scaling and CDC. Extensions (PostGIS, pgvector, TimescaleDB) extend functionality massively. VACUUM manages dead tuple cleanup; partitioning handles large tables.
use: Transactional OLTP requiring strong ACID guarantees and complex joins
Geospatial data with PostGIS (standard for location-aware systems)
Hybrid relational + document with JSONB columns
Multi-purpose database (with pgvector for small-scale vector search)
avoid: Write throughput beyond single-node vertical scaling (~5k writes/sec ceiling before sharding)
Global distributed active-active across regions (CockroachDB/Spanner territory)
Analytical scans over billions of rows without columnar storage (use ClickHouse/warehouse)

props.max_connections: Connection ceiling (default ~100; use PgBouncer for pooling)
props.wal_level: minimal | replica | logical - controls replication and CDC capabilities

pat.d: Writes to primary, heavy reads to replicas.
Events written in same transaction as business data, polled by CDC or relay.

pits: Connection exhaustion without pooling - always use PgBouncer or built-in pooling in front
VACUUM bloat from long-running transactions preventing cleanup - monitor dead tuples
Replica lag causing stale reads for read-your-writes patterns - route to primary when needed
tips: Extensions are PostgreSQL's superpower - mention PostGIS, pgvector, pg_cron as differentiators
Connection pooling is mandatory at scale - state the PgBouncer connection ratio rule of thumb
